title: Slackbot: icon to weekly recap
statusObserved: Meta card displayed Active; Library ID 1787295452461737; started Sep 1, 2026. This is an observation, not a performance claim.

hook.description: A cursor approaches the Slack icon; colored logo pieces lift and a real purple app window rises into the same focal area before one second.

scenes.title: Open the product
scenes.visual: Slack app icon on pale lilac, followed by the purple desktop window.
scenes.motion: Cursor approach, logo breakup and upward window reveal.
scenes.purpose: Recognizable brand action replaces a static logo slate.

scenes.title: Enter a personal workspace
scenes.visual: App shell fills with Slackbot greeting and a small existing-context card.
scenes.motion: Window settles, content resolves, then a rapid push-in.
scenes.purpose: Connect the opening icon to the working product.

scenes.title: Put the request above its user
scenes.visual: Split composition: executive interview below, a card carrying her weekly-recap request above.
scenes.motion: Hard cut into split layout; text appears inside a persistent request card.
scenes.purpose: Attach a concrete task to a visible practitioner.

scenes.title: Show the process
scenes.visual: Request remains while a channel-scanning indicator and Slackbot motif appear.
scenes.motion: Small progress-state animation above the interview; no full-screen wipe.
scenes.purpose: Bridge request to result without implying the result appeared before the request.

scenes.title: Deliver the same request
scenes.visual: A weekly team recap skill card replaces the process, followed by a cursor using it and a phone view below.
scenes.motion: Card replacement, cursor interaction, lower-panel cut to mobile.
scenes.purpose: Make the output object the focal point and show its use.

scenes.title: Human montage to brand
scenes.visual: Brief cuts through other people working, then the Salesforce mark.
scenes.motion: Fast live-action cuts and logo transition.
scenes.purpose: Broaden the situation after proof.

scenes.title: Destination
scenes.visual: Slack lockup, product URL and a purple get-started control.
scenes.motion: Text and CTA resolve, then hold.
scenes.purpose: Give one clear next step.

mechanism: The opening object becomes the app; the central request card then becomes the output card. Motion preserves a chain of meaning while the surrounding composition changes.
howWeApply: Todoist: keep the same sentence/task visible through recognition, click and Inbox result.
Tally: transform one meaningful form field into its saved response object.
Do not copy the testimonial, claimed ROI or branded logo animation.

title: One app, collaborative edits, chosen result
statusObserved: Motion archive labels this creative Active. Current Meta delivery and performance were not independently verified.

hook.description: A finished recipe app is already visible. Short action verbs accumulate above it while the app moves toward the camera; the opening is proof plus editing momentum.

scenes.title: Result first
scenes.visual: Recipe app preview floats over code panels on a dark ground; action-word heading accumulates.
scenes.motion: Sequential word highlighting, scrolling preview and an enlarging cursor.
scenes.purpose: Show what can be made before explaining tools.

scenes.title: Enter the working file
scenes.visual: Camera closes on the app toolbar and an open-file control.
scenes.motion: Strong push-in follows the cursor; browser chrome drops away.
scenes.purpose: Turn the advertised result into a working design object.

scenes.title: Explore together
scenes.visual: The same phone design expands into three alternatives, with named collaborator cursors.
scenes.motion: Pull back, duplicate and fan designs; cursors travel to different variants.
scenes.purpose: Visualize collaboration and variation without changing the core product object.

scenes.title: A visible local edit
scenes.visual: Macro crop of a cake illustration and edit controls.
scenes.motion: Cursor removes its background, then selects vectorization; the illustration changes.
scenes.purpose: Keep cause and changed pixels adjacent.

scenes.title: Second edit and screen
scenes.visual: A food image expands; camera moves across to a share-dialog design.
scenes.motion: Vertical image expansion followed by a lateral camera traverse.
scenes.purpose: Vary the camera because the task focus changes.

scenes.title: Return edited designs to the workflow
scenes.visual: Three app screens gather and an explicit send-to-Make action appears; the app views reconfigure.
scenes.motion: Pull-back, click emphasis, overlapping slides and reorder.
scenes.purpose: Close the loop from editing to an implemented preview.

scenes.title: Make a choice
scenes.visual: A board contains three alternatives; one is selected with a note.
scenes.motion: Camera zooms into the chosen option; a note lands on that design.
scenes.purpose: Show convergence after divergence.

scenes.title: Close with the product
scenes.visual: Return to dark app-and-code composition, then Figma mark.
scenes.motion: Match return to opening arrangement; short logo end card.
scenes.purpose: Reinforce the journey and identity.

mechanism: Object continuity supplies orientation across unusually large camera changes: result → editable asset → variations → edit → selected result.
howWeApply: Todoist: hook on a meaningful task object, then camera follows its date, time and priority rather than decorative orbiting.
Tally: use a changed field/response as the transition anchor.
Reserve wide views for orientation and macro views for real actions.

title: Conversation to a working site
statusObserved: Motion archive labels this creative Active. Current Meta delivery and performance were not independently verified.

hook.description: A living-room conversation is interrupted by a decisive move to the laptop around two seconds; the unknown idea becomes visible design work immediately afterward.

scenes.title: An idea in the room
scenes.visual: Two people sit talking in a living room.
scenes.motion: Subtle handheld framing and human gesture.
scenes.purpose: Set up an everyday collaboration situation; spoken premise was not audited.

scenes.title: Act on the idea
scenes.visual: A person pulls the laptop forward; the next shot shows two animal-logo sketches in Figma.
scenes.motion: Action cut from person to screen.
scenes.purpose: Convert conversation into tangible design evidence.

scenes.title: Build in quick details
scenes.visual: Close shots alternate between hands, a collaborator face, and a poster layout.
scenes.motion: Short hard cuts with tight crops.
scenes.purpose: Show effort and progress through distinct useful details.

scenes.title: Prompt and reaction
scenes.visual: Figma prompt interface appears, followed by a person reacting.
scenes.motion: Cut to readable prompt area, then close-up reaction.
scenes.purpose: Bridge an idea to a generated artifact without requiring long explanatory text.

scenes.title: Working destination
scenes.visual: Laptop shows a complete nickname-themed site with heading and input.
scenes.motion: Cut to site, small camera motion and a brief readable hold.
scenes.purpose: Reveal the actual output as payoff.

scenes.title: Finished gesture
scenes.visual: Laptop closes; its sticker stays in view.
scenes.motion: Physical closure matches narrative closure.
scenes.purpose: Signal completion with a real object action.

scenes.title: Identity
scenes.visual: Figma mark on black.
scenes.motion: Hard cut, static hold.
scenes.purpose: Brand close.

mechanism: Physical action motivates every cut: idea spoken, laptop pulled in, work performed, site revealed, laptop shut. The hook does not need unrelated animation.
howWeApply: Todoist: make the opening obstruction clear because the task enters the product, not as decorative footage.
Linear: a real issue-state change can motivate a camera cut as decisively as the laptop movement.

title: Paper obstruction to applied rewrite
statusObserved: Motion archive labels this creative Active. Current Meta delivery and performance were not independently verified.

hook.description: A sheet held across the lens tears away during the first half second, revealing the speaker while a concise writing-friction subtitle remains visible.

scenes.title: Tear away the obstruction
scenes.visual: Notebook paper blocks most of a speaker; it is pulled/torn away.
scenes.motion: Fast physical foreground wipe.
scenes.purpose: Create immediate visible change related to writing.

scenes.title: Name the friction
scenes.visual: Speaker talks directly to camera with one problem subtitle.
scenes.motion: Tight handheld portrait and small gestures.
scenes.purpose: Give the attention-grab a relevant problem.

scenes.title: Identify the tool
scenes.visual: Laptop views show Grammarly and writing-assistance feature cards.
scenes.motion: Hard cuts, physical push-in and small camera sway.
scenes.purpose: Move from problem to actual software rather than a long slogan.

scenes.title: Enter the writing
scenes.visual: Email composition is selected and a writing-assistant panel opens.
scenes.motion: Cut to the message, cursor selection, tool panel appears.
scenes.purpose: Locate the precise text being improved.

scenes.title: Apply the result
scenes.visual: A rewrite suggestion is shown and accepted; changed email text remains visible.
scenes.motion: Panel-to-text change inside the same email crop.
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate completion instead of stopping at a suggestion.

scenes.title: Single CTA
scenes.visual: Grammarly logo and a green download control on black.
scenes.motion: Simple entrance and a long end hold.
scenes.purpose: Clear action, though the hold is longer than our short-film target.

mechanism: The hook is a content-relevant obstruction/removal, followed quickly by a small but complete before/action/after proof.
howWeApply: Todoist: use a legible thought block that clears into the same task sentence.
Keep our authentic recognition and saved Inbox row; do not replace proof with a reveal alone.
Borrow the interruption and semantic handoff, not the speaker, paper footage or claims.

title: A spoon workshop becomes a poster
statusObserved: Motion archive labels this creative Active. Current Meta delivery and performance were not independently verified.

hook.description: Hands carve a spoon, then the finished spoon is held toward the lens; the creator pivots to making the workshop poster. The viewer sees the purpose before software.

scenes.title: Show the real work
scenes.visual: Close view of a woodcarving tool and spoon on a workbench.
scenes.motion: Hand action and tight crop.
scenes.purpose: Start with the audience’s activity, not a software logo.

scenes.title: Connect object to need
scenes.visual: Finished spoon is presented; creator turns toward laptop and poster-making heading appears.
scenes.motion: Object approaches lens, then gesture-led turn.
scenes.purpose: Tie the design task to a concrete event.

scenes.title: Gather visual direction
scenes.visual: Creator at a table; several inspiration posters overlay the shot.
scenes.motion: Hard cut; reference images appear sequentially then clear.
scenes.purpose: Explain what the following design is based on.

scenes.title: Bring an image into the editor
scenes.visual: Laptop shows Canva, an inspiration poster and separate selected components.
scenes.motion: Push from wide laptop view to screen; selection outlines reveal parts.
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate the relevant editing mechanism.

scenes.title: Make it the creator’s own
scenes.visual: Poster typography and color change; a spoon graphic replaces the central illustration.
scenes.motion: Edits remain on one persistent canvas; camera cuts closer.
scenes.purpose: Keep the visual identity of the work while showing meaningful customization.

scenes.title: Finish and animate
scenes.visual: The blue spoon-workshop poster is adjusted and animated in the editor.
scenes.motion: Small changes followed by a larger final poster view.
scenes.purpose: Show a completed artifact after the edit sequence.

scenes.title: Show the output at useful scale
scenes.visual: Final poster overlays the returning creator.
scenes.motion: Large centered artifact replaces tiny editor view.
scenes.purpose: Let the viewer read the result.

scenes.title: Invitation and tool CTA
scenes.visual: Creator gestures with a try-the-feature prompt and event invitation.
scenes.motion: Overlay clears to the person; short end gesture.
scenes.purpose: Close on the original real-world purpose.

mechanism: Purpose → original material → working canvas → customized deliverable. The object introduced in the hook returns inside the final output.
howWeApply: Tally: begin with a concrete event/signup need, then let the same details become the form and response.
Todoist: preserve one thought all the way to the scheduled task; do not rotate through unrelated sample tasks.

title: Finished poster first, editable proof second
statusObserved: Motion archive labels this creative Active. Current Meta delivery and performance were not independently verified.

hook.description: A dramatic finished poster occupies the frame immediately. Its planes separate, then editor selection bounds appear and the headline becomes editable within the first three seconds.

scenes.title: Reveal the finished artifact
scenes.visual: A cinematic portrait poster with bold red type fills the view; foreground planes separate slightly.
scenes.motion: Short depth/fan reveal then flattening.
scenes.purpose: Present a desirable output before the process.

scenes.title: Prove editability
scenes.visual: Same poster in Canva; text and image are selected and the headline changes.
scenes.motion: Selection rectangles and direct text edit.
scenes.purpose: Make the output feel controllable, not merely generated.

scenes.title: Second artifact, same affordance
scenes.visual: Another cinematic poster appears with selected portrait elements and type controls.
scenes.motion: Match cut to a second design; zoom out to app window.
scenes.purpose: Show the same editing mechanism on a different artifact.

scenes.title: Return to the beginning
scenes.visual: Browser URL and Canva home interface are shown.
scenes.motion: Quick application-window replacement and push-in.
scenes.purpose: Rewind from result to a reproducible starting point.

scenes.title: Prompt to options
scenes.visual: Prompt is entered; response with several poster options appears; camera picks one.
scenes.motion: Text entry, generated-results reveal and a quick push into an option.
scenes.purpose: Connect the initial output to a request.

scenes.title: Edit the chosen poster
scenes.visual: Persistent poster canvas; image elements and type are selected and several typefaces tested.
scenes.motion: Local edits with small camera drift.
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate control, but this long middle is an editorial pacing limitation.

scenes.title: Another controlled variation
scenes.visual: Return to the first poster; headline, text color and layout adjustments are visible.
scenes.motion: Match cut back; incremental edits in the same editor view.
scenes.purpose: Reinforce editable components rather than a one-shot result.

scenes.title: Finished-output montage
scenes.visual: Three full-screen posters appear with a short tool CTA.
scenes.motion: Fast outcome cuts and final hold.
scenes.purpose: Close on output quality.

mechanism: Outcome-first sequencing is paired with immediate editable bounds, then a process rewind. The first three seconds supply both ambition and proof.
howWeApply: Tally: show a filled, useful response object first, then pull back to the field that creates it.
Todoist: allow the thought typography to become a real input rather than keeping it as an unrelated headline.
Avoid importing the lengthy font-menu exploration into an 18-second film.
